podcast.title: Formation as Songwriting Vehicle (1986)
podcast.body: Carl Wallinger formed World Party in 1986 specifically to serve as an outlet for his songwriting. "Walinger put that band together in 1986 as a vehicle for his songwriting."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Alternative Album Grammy Nominee (1991)
podcast.body: World Party was one of the inaugural nominees for the "Alternative Album" Grammy category when it was introduced in 1991, signifying their early prominence within the alternative music scene. "The first nominees were Kate Bush, the replacements, World Party, and Laurie Anderson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Alternative Album Grammy Nominee (1991)
xref.body: Kate Bush was among the initial nominees for the "Alternative Album" Grammy category when it was first introduced in 1991. This marked a significant step in the formal recognition of alternative music by the Recording Academy. "The first nominees were Kate Bush, the replacements, World Party, and Laurie Anderson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Alternative Album Grammy Nominee (1991)
xref.body: The Replacements were included in the first group of nominees for the "Alternative Album" Grammy category when it was established in 1991. This nomination represented early institutional acknowledgment of the alternative genre. "The first nominees were Kate Bush, the replacements, World Party, and Laurie Anderson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Ongoing History Book of Firsts

xref.title: First Alternative Album Grammy Nominee (1991)
xref.body: Laurie Anderson was among the first artists to be nominated in the "Alternative Album" Grammy category when it debuted in 1991. Her nomination highlighted the diverse range of artists being recognized in this new genre classification. "The first nominees were Kate Bush, the replacements, World Party, and Laurie Anderson."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Another Roadside Attraction Festival (1993)
xref.body: The Tragically Hip organized the festival "Another Roadside Attraction" in 1993, 1995, and 1997. This festival was one of several Canadian-based summer music events during the 90s, showcasing the growing strength and popularity of domestic music. "There was another roadside attraction, which was organized by the Trajically Hip in 1993, 1995 and 1997."
